explanation: Brazil needed only a draw in the last match at the Maracanã and led 1-0, but Schiaffino and Ghiggia scored to give Uruguay a 2-1 win, often remembered as the final.

claims.text: The 1950 World Cup was decided by a final round-robin group of four teams, with no final match.
The 1950 title was not decided by a two-legged final, a penalty shoot-out or drawing lots.
Before the last match of the 1950 final group, Brazil needed only a draw to win the title.
In that match at the Maracanã on 16 July 1950, Friaça put Brazil 1-0 ahead, and Schiaffino and Ghiggia scored to give Uruguay a 2-1 win and the title.
